title: Duel-Evolve: Reward-Free Test-Time Scaling via LLM Self-Preferences

mechanism.domainTask: Test-time mathematical reasoning and competitive-programming code generation
mechanism.populationDetail: An evaluated candidate pool and confidence-pruned survivor subset are maintained for each problem, with no islands or tree backbone.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The confidence survivor subset filters active candidates but is not a separate elite archive.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Batched children enter the pool; appendix caps it at 200 and applies confidence pruning while comparison history remains available.
mechanism.generationDetail: Each evolved response synthesizes improvements from five or six scored parent solutions; initial candidates are generated from the problem alone.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Code public-test traces are coarse prompt context, whereas pairwise self-preference remains the primary optimization signal.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Five parents for code and six for math; selection operates on confidence-pruned survivor pool.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Preference-duel posterior with confidence pruning and mixed parent selection; its inferred scalar utilities are not external reward scores.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/DUEL-EVOLVE REWARD-FREE TEST-TIME SCALING VIA LLM SELF-PREFERENCES.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Survey currently cites preference evaluation and Gemma use; method also supports population, multi-parent prompting, repeated/parallel evaluation, and posterior-adaptive control. Pool cap/pruning qualifies incremental insertion. Verbal feedback reuse is explicit for code but not math.
